articles.title: Spider-Man Meets Luke Skywalker in New Look at Marvel x Star Wars Crossover, Even if the Line Makes My Brain Break
articles.summary: Marvel Comics and Star Wars are crossing over and Spider-Man's first line to Luke Skywalker is exactly the kind of thing we want from this story. When Disney bought Star Wars in 2012, fans knew it would only be a matter of time before the two franchises would cross over. Since the August announcement of […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Marvel Comics and Star Wars are crossing over and Spider-Man's first line to Luke Skywalker is exactly the kind of thing we want from this story. When Disney bought Star Wars in 2012, fans knew it would only be a matter of time before the two franchises would cross over. Since the August announcement of Star Wars/Marvel: Hope Assembles #1 , Marvel has been feeding fans scenes from the book to hype them up, with the latest revealing an X post revealing Spider-Man's first line to Luke Skywalker. Because it's Spider-Man, written by Kevin Smith, we get an awesome reference to A New Hope.

Smith is a longtime Marvel and Star Wars fans, including both in his work. One of the most famous parts of his first movie Clerks was when Dante and Randall discussed the realities of building the second Death Star, so fans were ready for this comic to be full of Star Wars references of all kinds. Smith's Spider-Man has always been one of the funnier versions of the hero and let's be real – if Peter Parker met Luke Skywalker, he would speak to him almost exclusively through references to Star Wars . Smith and artist David Marquez bring ths to life, as the Wall-Crawler drops a line on Luke that will be very familiar to fans.

Spider-Man is the everyman superhero . That's always been the appeal of the character. Back in the '60s, readers could see themselves in him and that has gone on for decades. Peter Parker was a nerdy kid who almost certainly watched Star Wars religiously and would definitely fanboy out if he met the young Jedi hopeful. The story, which is being kept mostly under wraps features the heroes of the Marvel Universe being pulled into the Star Wars Universe. The comic is meant to coincide with the 50th anniversary of the first film and most of the art we've seen from Marquez looks like the story is based during the time frame of Star Wars: Episode IV – A New Hope .

Spidey dropping Luke's classic line to Leia from the detention deck scene is a super fun piece of dialgoue, and exactly what readers have come to expect from Smith. Smith's movies made geek culture cool in the '90s and he has served as one of the greatest ambassadors for comics and sci-fi ever since. Smith is honestly the perfect person to write this comic, because he can make moments like this feel real.

There's a very killjoy way of looking at this moment, but think about it – if you were a kid who grew up watching Star Wars (and I don't know why I'm saying if here, you definitely did) and got a chance to take part in the events of Episode IV, you'd definitely do something like this. Smith is getting to write Spider-Man saying a Luke Skywalker line to Luke and it's one of those pop culture moments you can only get from Marvel Comics. There's an argument to be made this comic is going to be so jam-packed with moments like this that it's not even going to be a story, to which I have one thing to say – let people have fun.

Crossovers like this are supposed to be fun. Sure, there's almost certainly going to be some kind of overarching plot to this book, but the real fun for readers is getting moments like this. We all want a story that makes sense, sure, but we also want to get some amazing moments just like this one. It's getting to play Peter Parker as a Star Wars fan saying classic lines to the characters. I hope we get more moments like this from this crossover; I want Spider-Man to annoy everyone by quoting their own lines back at them.

For example, with this scene, did Luke already rescue Leia and said this line? When Spidey regurgitates it to him, does he realize that the hero is just quoting him? It's questions like this that make these kinds of moments so great. It's like geek Inception and the more I think about it, the more my brain spins off into the Shadow Realm. Crossovers like this aren't supposed to be taken seriously, they're supposed to be fun and this one looks like it's going to be a blast.

Seeing Spidey quote Luke Skywalker lines back at him is one of those things that I never knew I wanted to Kevin Smith to write, but now that I know it's a thing, I want more of it. There's a part of me that sees this for the cynical sales ploy it is, but it's moments like this that make these sorts of stories so fun. We've had lots of crossovers of all kinds over the years, but never before have we had one of this scale, with the potential for this kind of referential humor. Does it break your brain a little to think about? Sure. Is it fun as all get out? Of course it is.

Star Wars/Marvel: Hope Assembles #1 is on sale January 13, 2026.

Do you think moments like this are going to be awesome or do you think they'll hold the story back? What other lines would you like to see Spider-Man quote at people? Sound off in the comment section below.

articles.title: GTA 6 - How To Fast Travel & Collect More Vehicles To Explore The World
articles.summary: Courtesy of Rockstar Games Navigating through Grand Theft Auto 6's world is a massive undertaking, with fast travel and stealing vehicles existing as far different systems than they've been in past titles. The series has undergone a variety of changes when it comes to open-world exploration, emphasizing new details players have to pay attention to if they want to […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Navigating through Grand Theft Auto 6 's world is a massive undertaking, with fast travel and stealing vehicles existing as far different systems than they've been in past titles. The series has undergone a variety of changes when it comes to open-world exploration, emphasizing new details players have to pay attention to if they want to get to new areas without too much trouble. Having an arsenal of vehicles at your disposal can help you with this, but you still have to follow the right strategies to figure out the best ways to travel across the island of Leonida.

Sometimes it costs a little money to make travel easier in GTA 6 , whether it's in your control or not. You might have to progress through the game's early stages a bit to make travel smoother, either by building up enough cash to buy the fastest cars you want, or to have a disposal income you can use on paying other services to ferry you to different locations. Stealing cars is much harder in GTA 6 than past games in the series, so you have to be ready to acquire other means of transportation than just forcing yourself into whatever vehicle you see parked or driving on the road.

You can't just teleport to places you want whenever you want in GTA 6 , whether you discover certain locations or not on your map. Fast travel doesn't exist within the game as it does in others, as you need to pay for the convenience of skipping long trips around Leonida's various sub-regions. For example, you can pay for a service to drive you from one place to another, but the entire drive will be played out depending on who you call. To travel at a much faster rate, here are some ways you can ignore the tedium of such a drawn-out road trip:

The RydeMe service is perhaps the most reliable way to "fast travel," although it might also be the most expensive way to do so. This is the premier taxi company in GTA 6 , costing a small amount to go from point A to point B, with players able to speed up the taxi driver by paying an additional $5 as they go. While it's funny to see the chaotically inventive ways in which a taxi driver will overcome traffic, the novelty of that mayhem can wear off fast. Should you want to have the entire trip skipped and mimic the teleportation of other games' fast travel systems, all you have to do is pay the RydeMe driver $100 to leap to your destination.

This amount might cost more depending on the length of the trip, so be prepared to spend some cash. Harming your RydeMe driver will prevent you from booting up the app for awhile, so it may not be a good idea to put them in harm's way. You also have to be close to a road to call a RydeMe driver, though at that point, you may as well just find a nearby bus stop. Using public transport like a bus or train is less expensive, but the stations for each are harder to find on the map. You'll also have to wait for the vehicle to arrive, and can only travel between stops they are stationed for.

Thankfully, taking a train or bus will allow you to press "Skip Journey" in its menu, similar to the RydeMe taxi. This skips the trip entirely through a fade to black, essentially teleporting you to the next listed stop. On the other hand, you could have a faster, personal vehicle delivered to you using the Scooter Bros service through another app on your phone. This group will charge you for the distance it takes to deliver a vehicle, but paying for their premium service can skip that extra charge. Alternatively, you could manipulate GTA 6 's spawning system with Jason or Lucia, resetting the game or swapping to either character as they organically exist in different parts of the same world.

Many players might imagine that the best way to avoid paying for "fast travel" services is to steal the nicest, fastest car in GTA 6 and store it for themselves. While you certainly still can commit grand theft auto in Grand Theft Auto , the process is made deliberately harder, with stolen vehicles being almost impossible to keep for yourself. Players are able to smash car windows and fight drivers to break into cars, yet this will often alert authorities in new ways than the series has seen before. Cars are easier to track, and some of them have built-in alarms that blare out and draw attention once stolen.

When you get the "Waink It" app on your phone in Chapter 1 of GTA 6 , you can scan cars to see their make and model, as well as other useful features. This will help you greatly in stealing anything, as you can see if a car is locked, alarmless, or whether it requires physical keys at all. Registering a car at the Pay N' Spray shops is how you take ownership of them, but this can become a complicated process if you aren't used to it. The more expensive the car, the more it might take to steal it, from cloning digital keys to hotwiring engines with different resources. As such, it isn't always reliable to use a stolen getaway as your means of fast travel.

Once you reach Chapter 2 of GTA 6 , you'll unlock a Garage you can use to store your vehicles, stolen or otherwise. That being said, there are multiple Garages you can purchase all around the map, with each ranging in price when listed on the Vice City Real Estate app you can pull up on your phone. Every new Garage is a new space to store an important vehicle for faster travel, with each being something you're able to call to your side through the Scooter Bros service mentioned earlier. Yet, having other vehicles stored and ready can help you navigate all sorts of terrain, up to the very skies and seas that block off certain areas of the map.

Motorcycles and bikes are vehicles you can steal, with boats being something you can own at much later points of the game. If you own the Ultimate Edition of GTA 6 , Chapter 4 even starts off with allowing you to get a Shitzu Squalo boat in preparation for the game's story. At the same time, planes are something you can acquire too, those boats and planes are typically only obtained when you clone keys to steal them. Much like cars, the more advanced the vehicle, the harder it is to take for yourself. There is no way to register a boat or plane for your character at this time of writing, but this could change as the game evolves with future updates.

At the end of the day, fast travel is ironically subjective in Rockstar's latest blockbuster, usually defined by how far you're willing to go to make navigation easier. Illegal or legal means can be costly, creating different levels of risk as you learn to efficiently explore every region on the Leonida map. As far as Grand Theft Auto 6 's systems go, it's mostly up to player creativity to determine what "fast travel" looks like for them, with that definition changing as they discover new ways to collect vehicles of all kinds.

What is your favorite way to travel throughout GTA 6 so far? Let us know in the comments below!

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Friday the 13th fans finally received the news they have been waiting more than 15 years to hear with the announcement that Jason Voorhees will return to cinemas in a new movie in 2027 . Following the success of Peacock prequel series Crystal Lake , which focuses on Jason Voorhees' mother Pamela in the years before her killing spree that began the franchise, the Jason Universe venture (the rights issues with the franchise have created two separate entities with their finger in the Voorhees pie) is now pushing ahead with a movie from Friday the 13th veteran Steven Miner. While fans digest that information, a new auction from Heritage Auctions can help anyone with deep pockets to grab their own piece of Jason's past with the sale of Kane Hodder's screen-used mask from Jason Goes to Hell: The Final Friday.

While the Friday the 13th movies have never really managed to get above ground-level as far as critics are concerned, Jason Goes to Hell is regarded as one of the worst films in the entire saga…with good reason. Although it seemed impossible to sink lower than Friday the 13th Part VIII: Jason Takes Manhattan - which unlike its title suggests could have been called "Jason Spends a Lot of Time Killing People on a Cruise Ship Before Spending 15 minutes in Manhattan" - in 1993 that happened with the "final" outing for the ultimate mother's boy. In Jason Goes to Hell , the movie opens with Jason being completely obliterated after being trapped by authorities - although there is no explanation how he is alive at all after his watery demise in the previous movie. From here, Jason hardly features in the film as his evil soul takes over the body of one officer and goes about bringing himself back to life in his own body. The movie's meandering and disjointed plotting did it no favors, and it seemed like this was very much the end of the line for Jason.

As the 9th movie in a franchise that never pleased anyone in terms of storytelling but managed to keep its head above water with creative kills and an iconic killer , Jason Goes to Hell appeared to be the final nail in the coffin for Friday the 13th . Yet, it's cheeky tease of a crossover with A Nightmare on Elm Street eventually became a reality over a decade later, by which time Jason had already been revived and sent to space to become a killer cyborg. In 2009, Friday the 13th was given a bright and shiny new reboot with a remake, but then fell foul of multiple claims over who owned which parts of the franchise, and that was a tangled web that even Jason couldn't machete his way out of easily. Now, with the rights split between two parties, Friday the 13th is rebooting itself again for more bloody mayhem.

Regardless of what happens in the future of the franchise, the past is full of nostalgia and that is something that pulls fans towards props and other memorabilia when they appear at auction. That is why the mask worn by Kane Hodder in his final appearance as Jason, and his own copy of the film's first script, are now set to sell for at least $40,000. Owning a piece that was worn by Hodder, who is regarded by many as the best Jason performer to have been behind the mask , is a chance that does not come up every day, so that price will probably push even higher by the end of the auction. Before a new mask is forged, why not treat yourself to something old while you wait.

Was Jason Goes to Hell the worst movie of the Friday the 13th franchise? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title: Steam Machine Price Increase Likely Coming Very Soon, Says Valve
articles.summary: Valve has indicated that it will likely have to increase the price of its Steam Machine platforms in the future. Prior to launching earlier this year, Valve was forced to indefinitely delay the Steam Machine due to manufacturing costs that continued to prompt the company to reevaluate how much it would sell its new hardware […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Valve has indicated that it will likely have to increase the price of its Steam Machine platforms in the future. Prior to launching earlier this year, Valve was forced to indefinitely delay the Steam Machine due to manufacturing costs that continued to prompt the company to reevaluate how much it would sell its new hardware for . Eventually, it settled on a pricing scheme that saw the 512GB model going for $1,049, with the 2TB version selling for $1,349. And while these prices have continued to hold firm since release, they might not for much longer.

In a new blog post on Steam , Valve talked about what's next for the Steam Machine. Starting this week, Valve said that the 512GB edition of the Steam Machine no longer has a waitlist, which means that anyone looking to buy it can simply head to the product's website and purchase one without an invite. For the 2TB model, however, Valve said it still has more people on the device's waitlist than it does units to sell. Because of this, Valve explained that it now has to manufacture more Steam Machine units before they can put them up for sale, but once it does this, it could lead to price changes for the platform.

"We are continuing to build more Steam Machine units, but memory and storage costs continue to increase at unprecedented levels; as a result we don't yet know the number we are able to make, and at what price we'll be able to offer them," Valve said. "The 2TB model in particular will be especially constrained."

While this is all a bit disappointing to hear from Valve, the company warned as much back in July that the cost of the Steam Machine would likely end up going up. In fact, Valve is far from alone in being forced to increase the cost of its products, as companies like PlayStation, Xbox, and Nintendo have all done the same over the past year as well.

As for when these potential price changes for the Steam Machine would go into effect, Valve said that it will share more details in January. This indicates that a price hike would likely happen around the same time, as Valve almost certainly wouldn't want to delay an increase for very long. With this in mind, if you happen to have an invite to purchase the 2TB Steam Machine now, or you simply are willing to settle for the 512GB version, you might want to pull the trigger sooner rather than later.

How do you feel about the Steam Machine becoming even pricier in the future? And will this warning from Valve prompt you to pick up the device now? Be sure to let me know for yourself in the comments below.
